goal: Make CBlockIndex pointer parameters into references in places where null is never valid.
Aims to make non-null invariants explicit and reduce future null-pointer bugs.
Touches chain/CChain internals, net_processing block-download logic, and block filter index lookups.
reviewability: Stale: author has not pushed or commented since 2026-05-27, well past the 60-day silence threshold.
Reviews so far (concept ACKs) are on earlier revisions; the CChain reference_wrapper change is the newest and least reviewed part.
agreement: Strong: three concept ACKs with musaHaruna giving a substantive rationale about compile-time non-nullability guarantees (stickies-v, musaHaruna, w0xlt).
Author responded to and resolved nit and design comments from stickies-v, musaHaruna, and maflcko, including reworking the CChain storage approach per maflcko's suggestion.
No open objections remain in the visible discussion.

result.summary: This PR is a continuation of #34440, changing several CBlockIndex* parameters to const CBlockIndex& references where null is never a valid input, across chain.h/cpp, net_processing.cpp, index/base.cpp, and index/blockfilterindex.cpp. The final commit changes CChain's internal vChain storage from std::vector<CBlockIndex*> to std::vector<std::reference_wrapper<CBlockIndex>>, a more invasive internal representation change. Public pointer-returning APIs are left unchanged. The stated motivation is improved code clarity and reduced risk of null-pointer bugs, not a functional fix.
result.problem: There is no reported bug; the PR addresses a latent, low-probability risk that future code changes could dereference a null CBlockIndex* where the contract guarantees non-null, which mainly benefits maintainers doing future refactors rather than users.

result.card: This PR continues #34440, converting several const CBlockIndex* parameters to const CBlockIndex& where null was never a valid input, across chain.h/cpp (LastCommonAncestor, CChain's internal vChain storage), net_processing.cpp (block-download helpers), and the block filter index lookup functions. It is a pure null-safety and clarity refactor with no reported bug, performance gain, or new feature; the author states the motivation is 'slight improvement in code quality, maintainability and robustness.' Three reviewers gave concept ACKs, with musaHaruna giving a substantive rationale about compile-time non-nullability guarantees, and the author addressed all review feedback including reworking CChain's storage to use std::reference_wrapper per maflcko's suggestion. The PR has had no author or reviewer activity since a June 2026 concept ACK from w0xlt, exceeding the staleness threshold, though nothing is known to be materially blocking review. Given its cleanup nature, it is low priority (P4) in every touched category (indexes, p2p, validation) since no concrete correctness hazard, bug, or performance issue is being retired.
